qualification: Ten complete sources inspected individually. Existing art retained. Source opinions are not atlas-cell, mounted, action, phone, child or all-jobs acceptance. One local sign-border concern remains in the inclusive refinement queue.

items.basis: The complete lavender shell doors, cream arch and grouped pearl/gold accents preserve the established palace vocabulary. Large shell grooves and a continuous symmetrical contour remain clear; soft shading is confined to broad bands. Retain this complete source. This inspection does not prove the mounted door size, clipping, opening interaction or a neighboring tile seam.

Three large pearl bubbles form one immediately readable bath symbol inside the cream/gold scalloped medal. The navy outer edge and grouped highlights match the other navigation badges. Retain; child recognition and mounted input/contrast remain separate checks.

A warm palette with four broad color dots and one diagonal brush communicates craft without text. The rounded medal, plum brush and small set of value bands match the palace signs. Retain the source; the brush is a navigation symbol, not proof of the actual craft action.

One large aqua droplet with a deep blue edge and broad white highlight reads clearly against the cream scalloped medal. The continuous silhouette and restrained detail match the bath/craft signs. Retain. Complete source review does not score its current doorway placement or route behavior.

The teddy face is warm, rounded and readable, with two complete ears and simple dark eyes/nose. At the upper middle of the medal, a short flat dark/tan fragment interrupts the otherwise scalloped cream/gold border. This is a local border-coherence concern inside the artwork, not a claim that the file edge clips the bear. Preserve the original and compare a clean existing badge or a targeted border repair; the inclusive 4.5 queue remains open. Current child recognition and mounted size have not been accepted.

Grouped pearl/gold horizontal bands and two large blue door arches sit on a quiet lavender masonry field. The broad values distinguish entrances without competing with their future signs. This exact tile is a crop of the continuous hall; cut arches at the lower tile boundary are expected, not standalone defects. Retain; evaluate assembled seams and per-screen native coverage separately.

One blue doorway and a cream column continue the same lavender masonry and pearl trim. Column shading stays broad enough for the toy-palace language. The partial stair arch at the right edge belongs to the neighboring panorama area. Retain the exact tile; no seam, panorama coverage or doorway interaction pass follows from source inspection.

The lower portions of two blue doorways lead onto a lavender floor and a broad red carpet. Warm trim and restrained reflections preserve the established hall staging. Small floor texture remains subordinate to the route. Retain this exact lower tile; pair its top edge with the actual upper tile before assigning an assembled-background score.

The blue doorway, cream column base, stair edge and uninterrupted red carpet continue the same hall vocabulary. Broad floor reflections stay legible without a new realistic lighting treatment. Retain this exact lower tile. Neighboring seams, scaling, card joins and the current actor/door composition remain unscored.

Eight complete illustrated water stages use deep blue contours, large aqua value bands and rounded white foam/drops. The rise and collapse have a coherent graphic water identity. The unused ninth grid space is not an authored action frame and is not a weak asset. Retain the whole atlas. This whole-source opinion does not assign scores to individual cells or establish their playback order, contact scale or continuous action quality.
